indicators.text: AI approval is treated as proof that the code is secure.
Nobody can explain the authentication or authorization flow without asking the AI again.
Tests cover generated happy paths but not denied or malicious cases.
A package was installed because the AI named it, without registry or maintainer verification.
A security warning was removed by disabling the check rather than fixing or accepting the risk explicitly.
Client-side hiding or route secrecy is used as authorization.
Production secrets or dumps are exposed to the coding agent's context.
The coding agent has blanket shell, network, cloud or production privileges for routine tasks.
Untrusted issue, PR, log or web content is fed directly to an agent that can act on the repository.
CORS, storage, database or network exposure was widened until the application started working.
A large AI-generated diff is merged without understanding unrelated changes.
The same AI generation loop is the only reviewer and test author for security-critical code.
No one knows which version/configuration was actually deployed.
There is no tested rollback or recovery path for a bad release or destructive data change.
Security findings are suppressed without a named owner and rationale.
The product is public even though critical controls remain UNKNOWN or merely CLAIMED.
